title: Model pinning onboarding cues and copy playbook
body:
Purpose and scope:
This doc collects lightweight wireframe notes, microcopy variants, acceptance criteria, and a short grooming backlog for the model 'pin' onboarding experience in the Console. Target: engineers + PM + design to implement a low-friction, discoverable path for new and existing users to fix an endpoint to a specific model version (pin), understand consequences, and recover from failures.

Design goals (high level):
- Make pinning explicit and reversible. Avoid accidental version lock-in.
- Surface key tradeoffs: stability vs. cost/latency/regression risk.
- Provide progressive disclosure: minimal UI for quick flow, expandable details for power users.
- Be keyboard- and screenreader-friendly; visible focus states and clear ARIA labels.
- Instrument all consent/confirm steps to capture telemetry for future UX tuning.

Quick user stories:
- New developer: "I want my endpoint to always use the same model so my integration doesn't break when a new model ships."
- Platform owner: "I need to pin to a specific quantized variant for predictable unit cost."
- Ops: "If a pinned model regresses, I want a safe fallback and a quick rollback path."

Wireframe notes (textual sketches):
1) Catalog detail -> quick pin CTA (compact):
- Row-level affordance: small pin icon with tooltip "Pin version"; hover shows last 3 changes and a small caption: "Stable: last tested 2024-11-01".
- Clicking opens a compact sheet (right rail) with two columns: left = list of versions (ver, quant, perf badge), right = action panel + copy.
- Default action: "Pin to this version" (primary) and "Create endpoint with latest" (secondary).
- Microcopy above action: "Pinning locks endpoint to this model version. You can unpin or change later; rollback is supported."

2) Endpoint creation flow (pin step integrated):
- Stepper: 1) Endpoint basics 2) Model selection 3) Pin & rollout policy 4) Review
- In step 3 show toggle: [ ] Pin to version (off by default). When toggled on, reveal: dropdown of versions + small badge indicators (compatibility, quantization, cost delta).
- Inline copy variants (A/B):
  A: "Pin to this version to freeze model behavior. Useful for stable product integrations."
  B: "Lock behavior to this model version. You can unpin anytime — we'll keep a safe rollback history."
- Suggested default for slow-moving teams: show 'recommended' badge for currently pinned stable versions.

3) Confirmation / safety modal (when toggling pin on for an endpoint with live traffic):
- Title: "Pin endpoint to selected model version?"
- Body: "This will route all endpoint requests to model vX.Y. Live traffic may see different outputs and latency/cost. Rollbacks are supported but require a redeploy."
- Two CTA buttons: "Pin and Continue" (primary, red/orange accent) and "Cancel" (secondary).
- Secondary line: small link "Simulate potential diffs" that opens lightweight diff preview (see telemetry note).
- Accessibility: focus trap, aria-live region for success/failure.

4) Post-pinning state / UI affordances:
- Endpoint header displays pill: "Pinned: vX.Y" with tooltip "Click to change or unpin".
- Small inline changelog link "View pin history" leads to timeline with who/when and rollback button.
- If model variant is more expensive/higher latency show subtle warning: "Pinned model increases cost per token by ~12%" with link to cost calculator.

Microcopy bank (short lines for UI):
- Pin toggle label: "Keep endpoint on a fixed model version"
- Tooltip for pin icon: "Pin endpoint to this version — prevents auto-updates"
- Small status copy: "Pinned • vX.Y • 2024-11-01"
- Rollback CTA: "Rollback to previous pinned version"
- Unpin confirmation: "Unpin endpoint? Traffic will be routed to your routing policy (may be latest model)."

Copy variants for A/B testing (3 cells):
- Headline A: "Lock behavior with a model pin"
- Headline B: "Freeze the model driving this endpoint"
- Helper text A: "Pin keeps outputs stable across upstream model changes. Good for release-critical flows."
- Helper text B: "Use pin to avoid surprise changes from automatic model updates. You can unpin anytime."

Edge cases & error states (notes):
- Pin fails due to incompatible quantization: show inline error block: "Selected version incompatible with endpoint runtime. Try a compatible quantized variant or open a ticket." Include link to docs and 'Request compatibility' button.
- Attempt to pin when autoscaler policy blocks (e.g., not enough GPUs): show clear error with suggested actions: increase capacity, pick different variant, or schedule pin during maintenance window.
- If pinned model is deprecated/has CVEs: show high-severity banner and set a required reviewer flow for enterprise accounts.

Telemetry & analytics (events to emit):
- pin.initiated {user_id, endpoint_id, model_version, source_screen}
- pin.confirmed {user_id, endpoint_id, model_version, timestamp, a_b_variant}
- pin.cancelled {user_id, endpoint_id}
- pin.fallback_used {endpoint_id, original_version, fallback_version, reason}
- pin.rollback {user_id, endpoint_id, from_version, to_version}
- preview.diff_requested {user_id, endpoint_id, model_version}
Notes: include a boolean flag for 'enterprise_requires_review' in the payload to track friction. Keep events small to avoid PII.

Accessibility checklist (must-haves):
- Pin action keyboard tabbable; icons have aria-labels describing action.
- Modal dialogs trap focus and return focus to origin on close.
- Provide high-contrast badges for pinned state; avoid color-only statuses.
- Provide textual equivalents for diff preview (summary sentence for screenreaders).

Backlog grooming and implementation tasks (short prioritized list):
- P1: Compact right-rail version list + action panel (design + front-end + e2e) — CORE-1243.
- P1: Pin toggle in endpoint wizard with telemetry hooks — CORE-1251.
- P2: Confirmation modal + diff preview (backend endpoint to simulate sample inputs) — CORE-1260.
- P2: Pin history timeline + rollback API (backend + audit logs) — CORE-1272.
- P3: Cost delta estimator inline (calc service integration) — CORE-1290.
- P3: Enterprise review flow when pinning deprecated/unsafe models — SEC-413.

Acceptance criteria (for initial shipped MVP):
- UI shows a clear "Pin" affordance from catalog and endpoint creation.
- Toggling pin emits telemetry events and updates endpoint metadata.
- Users can unpin and rollback via timeline; rollback operation validated on staging.
- Confirmation modal displayed for pinned endpoints with live traffic; diff preview accessible.

Open questions / discussion points:
- Default: should pin toggle be off for endpoint creation? (Design leaning: off, to reduce accidental locking.)
- Should we autosuggest a pin for endpoints with integration tests that fail on model change? (Needs cross-team signal from CI/evals.)
- How to bake in multi-variant routing policies (percent rollout + pinned baseline)? UX complexity tradeoffs.

Quick copy notes for engineering handoff (tone + constraints):
- Tone: concise, neutral, confidence-building — focuses on developer control. Avoid alarmist language except for security/CVE cases.
- Length limits: badge labels <= 30 chars; one-line helper text <= 120 chars; modal body <= 280 chars.
- Internationalization: structure copy into small keys; avoid concatenating strings with variables in the middle of natural language.

Next steps (owners & short timeline):
- Design to produce final right-rail mocks (Ava, due 2024-11-15).
- Front-end spike to implement list + action panel (Ethan, due 2024-11-29).
- Backend endpoints for pin metadata & rollback (Miguel, due 2024-12-06).
- QA + accessibility pass (Priya, due 2024-12-13).

Notes to reviewers: please annotate copy lines you prefer by prefixing with [A] or [B]. If you think a line is too technical for the main flow, mark it as "advanced".

Appendix (short): sample API payload (pseudo):
- PATCH /endpoints/:id/pin {"model_version":"v3.2-qt8","force":false}
- Response 200: {"pinned_version":"v3.2-qt8","pinned_at":"2024-11-12T15:23:00Z"}

Scratch / quick brainstorm fragments (keep):
- "Pin advisory mode" — allow teams to mark a version as recommended without enforcing it.
- "Pin + Canary" — pin baseline while routing 5% to latest for gradual exposure.
- Microcopy idea: "Pinned. We'll keep a changelog for this endpoint so you can revert quickly."

End of document.
